effects: Pulls exactly `assets` USDC from the signer into the vault with transferFrom, which uses the signer's USDC allowance to the vault.
Mints previewDeposit(assets) yOG-USDC-V2 shares to `onBehalf`. The count comes from the share price after interest and fees accrue, and the call sets no minimum.
Moves the deposited USDC on to the liquidity adapter (Morpho). This moves none of the signer's assets.
formats.shown: Deposit an exact USDC amount into the yOG-USDC-V2 vault, with the shares going to the onBehalf address. The number of shares is not shown.

findings.title: deposit: the number of shares minted is not shown, and the call sets no minimum.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol deposit(): `uint256 shares = previewDeposit(assets);`. The share count is computed from storage (share price, fee shares) and is not in the calldata. Case 0: signer receives 9.742671890055489474 yOG-USDC-V2. The screen only shows 'Share ticker: yOG-USDC-V2'.
findings.fix: No descriptor change can show this. The 'Share ticker' field could be relabelled 'Receive shares (yOG-USDC-V2)' to make clear that shares arrive.

findings.title: deposit: the 'Share ticker' raw constant field is a bare ticker and does not say that shares are received.
findings.evidence: descriptor deposit field {label:'Share ticker', format:'raw', value:'$.metadata.constants.vaultTicker'} renders 'yOG-USDC-V2' on its own (case 0).
findings.fix: Use a label such as 'You receive shares of' or put it in the sentence: 'Deposit {assets} for yOG-USDC-V2 shares to {onBehalf}'.

cases.notes: The USDC out (10.064932) is shown exactly. The yOG-USDC-V2 shares in (9.74) go to the right address and are named by ticker, but no amount is shown. The vault decides the amount from storage.

formats.key: withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: Burns previewWithdraw(assets) yOG-USDC-V2 shares from `onBehalf` (rounded up). The call sets no maximum on the shares burned.
When the signer is not `onBehalf`, spends that many shares of onBehalf's share allowance to the signer.
Sends exactly `assets` USDC from the vault to `receiver`.
formats.shown: Withdraw an exact USDC amount to the receiver, with onBehalf shown as the owner. The number of shares burned is not shown.

findings.title: withdraw: the number of shares burned from the owner is not shown, and the call sets no maximum.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol withdraw(): `uint256 shares = previewWithdraw(assets);` then exit() `deleteShares(onBehalf, shares)`. Case 2: signer loses 112.037059253025828087 yOG-USDC-V2. The screen does not name shares at all.
findings.fix: No descriptor field can carry the share count. Optionally relabel 'Owner' to 'Burn vault shares of' so the signer knows yOG-USDC-V2 shares are spent.

cases.notes: The USDC in (115.714341, to the signer) is shown exactly. The shares out are only implied through the 'Owner' field, with no amount. The reader inferred that shares are burned.

formats.key: redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address onBehalf)
effects: When the signer is not `onBehalf`, spends `shares` of onBehalf's share allowance to the signer.
Sends previewRedeem(shares) USDC to `receiver` (rounded down). The call sets no minimum.
formats.shown: Redeem an exact number of yOG-USDC-V2 shares from the owner to the receiver. The screen never names the asset received (USDC) or its amount.

findings.title: redeem: the asset received (USDC) is never named, although the descriptor has it as a constant.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol exit(): `SafeERC20Lib.safeTransfer(asset, receiver, assets);` with asset = USDC (immutable 0x8335...2913). The redeem fields are only shares/To/Owner. Case 3: signer receives 42.21488 USDC. The reader wrote 'presumably USDC… inferred from the name only'.
findings.fix: Add a field {label:'Receive asset', format:'raw', value:'$.metadata.constants.underlyingTicker'} as mint does, and make the sentence 'Redeem {shares} for USDC to {receiver}'.

findings.title: redeem: the USDC amount received comes from the share price and the call sets no minimum.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol redeem(): `uint256 assets = previewRedeem(shares);`. It is not in the calldata, and losses or fee shares at accrueInterest can lower it.
findings.fix: None in the descriptor. A slippage-checked router would be needed.

cases.notes: The shares out (40.7928 yOG-USDC-V2) are shown exactly. The USDC in has neither asset nor amount on the screen. The reader guessed USDC from the vault name.

effects: Pulls previewMint(shares) USDC from the signer (rounded up) via transferFrom. The amount comes from the share price, and the call sets no maximum beyond the signer's allowance.
formats.shown: Mint an exact number of yOG-USDC-V2 shares to onBehalf, with 'Deposit asset: USDC' shown but no USDC amount.

findings.title: mint: the USDC amount pulled from the signer is not shown and has no maximum in the calldata.
findings.evidence: VaultV2.sol mint(): `uint256 assets = previewMint(shares); enter(assets, shares, onBehalf)` → `safeTransferFrom(asset, msg.sender, address(this), assets)`. Case 1: 0.913052 USDC left the signer, and the screen shows only 'Deposit asset: USDC'.
findings.fix: No descriptor change can show the amount. Label the field 'Pay with (amount set by vault price)' so the signer knows USDC leaves.

findings.title: mint: the intent 'Mint' and its sentence do not say that USDC leaves the signer's wallet.
findings.evidence: descriptor mint intent 'Mint', interpolatedIntent 'Mint {#.shares} for {#.onBehalf}'. Case 1 rendered 'Mint 0.9 yOG-USDC-V2 for 0x…dEaD', while the signer paid 0.913052 USDC.
findings.fix: Use intent 'Deposit USDC' and interpolatedIntent 'Deposit USDC to mint {#.shares} for {#.onBehalf}'.

cases.notes: The USDC out (0.913052) shows its asset but no amount. The minted shares went to 0xdead (signer null), and the screen showed that correctly.

mint(uint256 shares, address onBehalf).worst: mint: the intent 'Mint' and its sentence do not say that USDC leaves the signer's wallet.

summary.worst: redeem: the asset received (USDC) is never named, although the descriptor has it as a constant.
